industry: Auto insurance (local agents, captive and independent agencies, carriers)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'You'll save $X' or 'Save up to X%' without substantiation; savings averages must be described as averages among customers who switched and saved, with a disclaimer (FTC Sec. 5; carrier practice, SRC-PROG-CLAIMS).
'Best', 'cheapest', 'lowest rates' superlatives (unsubstantiable; carriers' own guides ban them).

'Is your auto insurance about to expire?' when you don't know the recipient's dates: it implies knowledge of their policy and can read as a notice from their insurer. Use 'Renewal coming up?' instead, or real renewal data with permission.
Look-alike 'renewal notice', 'policy notice', 'ATTENTION' formats styled like a carrier or DMV document (state unfair trade practices / misrepresentation; 39 USC 3001(h) if it implies government).
'Full coverage' as a promise (not a defined coverage; implies everything is covered).
Gift card or prize for getting a quote without checking the state's anti-rebating rule (NAIC Model 880 2020 amendment; caps vary by state).
Unsourced statistics; carrier names/logos you are not appointed with.
Unaudited vendor results (e.g., '7,604% ROI', '$360k LTV') printed as proof.
compliance_notes: State insurance unfair trade practices acts (based on NAIC Model 880) prohibit misrepresenting policy terms, benefits or the advantages of a policy, and false or misleading advertising.

Producer licensing: name the licensed agent/agency. California requires the license number on print ads distributed in CA, at least as large as any phone number or 12-pt, plus the word 'Insurance' (Ins. Code 1725.5). Check other states.

Carrier appointment/brand rules: captive agents (State Farm, Allstate, Farmers) usually must use carrier-approved templates and compliance review; independent agents may name only carriers they're appointed with.

Inducements: NAIC Model 880 (Dec 2020) allows non-cash gifts and raffles up to a commissioner-set reasonable amount, not unfairly discriminatory, with no purchase required. The drafting note suggests the lesser of 5% of premium or $250; states vary and some treat gift cards as cash.
Savings claims need substantiation before mailing (FTC Sec. 5) and state insurance ad rules; disclose basis (who saved, period, average).
Testimonials must be real customers with typical experience; material connections disclosed (16 CFR 255).
Telemarketing follow-up to mail responders falls under TSR/TCPA and state rules (not researched in depth here).
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, status, relief, nostalgia are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.
No age/demographic angle unless a cited source supports it for this industry; even then, check Fair Housing / ECOA before using it in housing or credit.

'Bring your declarations page - we'll match it line for line.'

emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: 'Save money' with no reason or proof (C-3PO AP-005 sameness); implying you know their expiration date.

emotion_by_offer.why: Uninsured drivers are a sourced risk (IRC 15.4%, 2023). Fear is legitimate here when paired with a single, easy action (EPPM).

'What happens if the other driver can't pay?'

emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Graphic crash photos with no clear action (EPPM denial); unsourced or stale statistics; implying the current policy is inadequate without knowing it.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 'Is your auto insurance about to expire?' (State Farm Billy Upton; 15,000 cards, 30 clients, vendor) vs misrepresentation rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: keep the timing idea but phrase it as a question that doesn't imply knowledge of the recipient's policy ('Renewal coming up?'), or use real permissioned renewal data.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 'Save up to 30%' / '7,604% ROI' templates vs FTC Sec. 5 substantiation and carrier savings-claim practice
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: savings only as substantiated averages among customers who saved, with basis; vendor ROI never printed.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gift-card drawings in gold (004, 008) vs state anti-rebating limits (NAIC 880)
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: non-cash or state-capped value, no purchase required, open to the public; verify state.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Progressive's brand guide avoids fear imagery for home coverage vs Patrick's emotion-agnostic rule
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Patrick's rule wins: the carrier guide is a brand choice, not law. Fear is allowed if the threat is true, sourced and paired with an easy action (EPPM).

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: FCA OP12 (verified RCT) found no motor effect from showing last year's premium vs vendor claims that renewal-timed mail works
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Verified study wins on that mechanism: don't rely on 'compare your old price' alone for auto; add a concrete done-for-you comparison offer. Timing remains reasonable but unproven.
